hypothesis: Asked on 2 Nov 2026: every model so far has been tested on the Laplace chain (and the Allen-Cahn field); test the same models on other chains whose kernels are known exactly, including 'real' first-order Markov processes. E61 runs one panel of arms on seven chains, all matched to E03's Laplace chain in variance (1) and lag-one correlation (0.85), so that a linear method sees the same covariance on every chain and every difference comes from shape: a Gaussian control (linear is optimal), Laplace (the anchor), Student-t and uniform innovations (inside the shift class), a skewed chain, and two textbook diffusions sampled at a fixed step, a double-well Langevin diffusion and the Student (Pearson) diffusion (outside it). The question is whether the kernel's advantage over the networks, and the ranking of the kernel families, are a property of the Laplace chain or of the method. The calibration from the true kernels says where the shift class must fail: its best member sits at 0.83 (skew), 0.98 (Langevin) and 0.86 (Pearson) of the linear floor, while the free mixture's reaches 0.16, 0.32 and 0.10; inside the class both are within 1-5% of it.
design: CHAINS (tools/core/calibrate_e61.py, true kernels only): gauss = GaussianAR1(0.85); laplace = LaplaceAR1(0.85); student = StudentTAR1(0.85, nu = 4) (the smallest of 3, 4, 5 with stationary mass beyond |a| > 8 below 1e-4); uniform = UniformAR1(0.85); skew: a = (sinh(asinh(z) + eps) - m)/s with z a Gaussian AR(1) of correlation r, eps = 0.744734 (marginal skewness 1), r = 0.858016 (lag-one correlation 0.85); langevin: dX = -V'(X) dt + sqrt(2) dW, V = 2 (x^2/s^2 - 1)^2 (barrier 2), s for variance 1, sampled every Delta = 0.307898; pearson: the Student diffusion dX = -X dt + sqrt(2 (nu + X^2)/(nu - 1)) dW with nu = 6 (rule as for student, among 5, 6, 8), standardised, sampled every Delta = 0.162369. The two diffusions' transitions are exact for the sampled process: square-root-approximation generator on the 0.02 lattice of [-12, 12] (detailed balance with the closed-form stationary law), matrix exponential over Delta, a sample sits uniformly inside its lattice cell. Every chain starts from a_1 ~ N(0, 1) (the package's convention; the diffusions snap it to its lattice cell), so the reference BP with the default initial law is exact. PROTOCOL: E57's (E03's): L = 32, the twelve frozen levels, grid 401 on [-8, 8], N in (32, 128, 512, 2048), seeds 0-7, 1024 validation and 2048 test chains per seed, E61's own tags e61-<chain>-train/val/test/em-split/em-noise; reference: exact grid BP with each chain's true kernel; floor (lmmse): the LMMSE of the chain's exact covariance on the same test bundle. ARMS: mixture (MixtureInnovationKernel, C = 8, E57's start), free4 (FreeMixtureKernel, C = 4, E60's), energy (NeuralEnergyKernel, width 16 = E56's screen winner, with fresh_on_reject), each by EM through exact grid BP from one noisy view per training chain (E56's _fit_and_select: E55's ladder to 2400, the checkpoint with the lowest pooled validation BP risk); energy_clean (the same kernel by clean-data maximum likelihood: E58's histogram Xi and the same M-step, the same ladder and selection); mlp and window (E03's screened winners, trained on the clean chains by E03's recipe, selected on the validation bundle). Driver: E57's helpers, chains and arms added in process; e57_chain_families.py byte-identical.

predeclared_predictions.P1: Control (gauss): every kernel arm (mixture, free4, energy, energy_clean) below both networks at every N, in >= 7/8 seeds each (paired).
predeclared_predictions.P2: Inside the shift class (laplace, student, uniform): the mixture below the window CNN at every N in >= 7/8 seeds, and at N = 2048 its seed-mean within 1.5x of the best of the three noisy-EM kernels (mixture, free4, energy) on every one of the three chains. (energy_clean is left out of this comparison: it learns from clean chains, a different information regime.)
predeclared_predictions.P3: Outside the shift class (skew, langevin, pearson): at N = 2048 free4 and energy each below the mixture in >= 7/8 seeds on every one of the three chains.
predeclared_predictions.P4: energy_clean below energy (noisy EM) at every N on >= 6 of the 7 chains, in >= 6/8 seeds at each N.
predeclared_predictions.P5: Generality: on every chain and at every N, the best kernel arm (the lowest seed-mean of the four) below the best network (the lower seed-mean of mlp and window) in >= 7/8 seeds (paired).

descriptive.D1: Seed-mean risk per chain x arm x N (raw E03 estimand; also / lmmse where the floor is above 1e-3).
descriptive.D2: kernel_hellinger of every kernel arm to the chain's true kernel at N = 2048.
descriptive.D3: E57's three chains (bimodal, tanh, hetero) joined to the panel through E57's frozen rows for the arms they share (mixture, mlp, window; E57's energy without the fresh-state rule, marked as such).
descriptive.D4: Selected checkpoints, at-cap shares and failed fits per arm.
descriptive.D5: Stalled energy fits (final lr below 1e-10) in energy and energy_clean: does the fresh-state rule hold?

predeclared_analysis: tools/core/read_e61.py. Gates: one row per (chain, seed, n_chains, arm, t), no duplicates; for every (chain, seed, n_chains) every arm, kernels and networks, scored on the same test bundle (hash). Risk = risk_pooled. A failed or missing fit counts AGAINST every prediction it enters: a seed-mean needs all eight seeds finite, a paired win needs both rows, 'best' is the lowest seed-mean among the arms that have one. No bootstrap, no other selection.
budget_rule: E55's ladder to 2400 EM iterations (or M-steps for energy_clean), no extension; E03's network budget.
